purpose: Secukinumab is used to treat certain conditions where your immune system is overactive, such as plaque psoriasis (a skin condition causing red, scaly patches), psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and other types of inflammatory arthritis. It helps reduce swelling, pain, and skin symptoms. Your doctor prescribed it to help control your immune system and improve your quality of life.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called IL-17A that, in some people, causes too much inflammation and attacks healthy tissue. Secukinumab is a special antibody that blocks this protein, like putting a cap on it so it cannot cause harm. By blocking IL-17A, the medication calms down the overactive immune response and reduces inflammation in your skin and joints.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include runny nose, sore throat, headache, diarrhea, and upper respiratory infections like colds. Some people may notice mild reactions at the injection site such as redness or itching. Yeast infections (like thrush in the mouth) can also occur more often while taking this medication.
warnings: Because this medication lowers part of your immune response, you are more likely to get infections, so tell your doctor right away if you have signs of infection like fever, chills, or unusual tiredness. Do not start this medication if you have an active infection. If you have inflammatory bowel disease (like Crohn's disease), talk to your doctor, as secukinumab may make it worse. Make sure all your vaccines are up to date before starting, and avoid live vaccines while on this drug. Always tell all your healthcare providers you are taking this medication.
typical_dosing: For most conditions, you start with a loading dose — usually one injection per week for 5 weeks — then switch to one injection every 4 weeks as a maintenance dose. Each injection is given under the skin (subcutaneously) using a prefilled pen or syringe. Your doctor or nurse will show you how to inject it at home. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing can vary depending on your condition.
